key_insight: Detonation spraying of Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C self-fluxing coatings is highly parameter-sensitive, with low barrel fill favoring dense low-friction coatings and higher O/C plus longer inter-shot delay improving wear resistance.
engineering_relevance: The results provide practical operating windows for restoring and hardening machine parts by balancing friction, hardness, porosity, and wear in sprayed coatings.
method: Varied barrel filling level (48–68%), O/C molar ratio (1.026–1.856), and inter-shot delay (0–1 s).
Characterized coating microstructure, thickness, porosity, and microcracks after detonation spraying.
Measured tribology, roughness, wear rate, friction coefficient, and hardness to identify optimal processing trade-offs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports friction as low as μ = 0.674 ± 0.136 at 48% fill and O/C = 1.026, while wear resistance peaked at O/C = 1.856 with 1 s delay, reducing specific wear rate to 0.000189 mm³/(N·m) and roughness from 5.00 to 3.60 μm.
watch_item: Optimizing for minimum friction can worsen wear, so process settings must be selected for the target service mode rather than a single best metric.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
